title: PTM-localization reanalysis module
context: Post-translational modifications (PTMs), especially phosphorylation, are central to cancer biology and many PRIDE cancer datasets include phospho-enrichment experiments. PTM-localization analysis (e.g., using Phospho-RS or MSFragger's PTMProphet) adds significant analytical complexity: site localization probabilities, localization FDR, and the interplay with peptide-level FDR all require additional validation. This is a methods-review-heavy addition to the pipeline. Re-identification risk from variant/SAV peptides must be assessed per the reid-policy before any proteogenomic search is attempted.
objective: Implement a PTM-localization module (starting with phosphorylation) for the reanalysis pipeline that produces site-localized, FDR-controlled PTM results with full provenance, validated on an approved open phospho-proteomics dataset.
acceptanceCriteria: A PTM-localization module (targeting phosphorylation as the primary PTM) is implemented within the Nextflow workflow, using a pinned tool (e.g., MSFragger/PTMProphet or equivalent) referenced by immutable container digest.
Site localization probabilities and localization FDR are computed and validated; the FDR/statistics harness is extended to cover PTM-localization FDR.

The module runs on an approved open phospho-proteomics dataset (passed allow-list gate: open-access, de-identified, license verified, re-id determined); re-identification risk from any proteogenomic search is assessed per reid-policy-006.
A complete run manifest is produced; 100% of published PTM-level assertions pass the CI provenance gate.
Pipeline code is MIT-licensed; aggregate tables are CC-BY-4.0; commit is DCO signed-off; pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
resources: proteomics-reanalysis-fdr-010 (FDR validation harness to extend for PTM-level FDR)
output: A committed PR containing the PTM-localization module, validated on an approved open phospho-proteomics dataset with complete run manifest and passing CI; code MIT, tables CC-BY-4.0.
